text: No export or import shall be made by any person without an Importer Exporter Code (IEC) number granted by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT). The IEC must be valid and accurately cited on all customs shipping bills and export commercial invoices.

Every exporter must register their 14-digit Authorised Dealer (AD) Code issued by their bank with the Indian Customs Electronic Gateway (ICEGATE) at the specific port of loading before filing an export shipping bill to enable customs clearance and export incentive processing.

rule_title: Statutory Entry of Goods for Exportation and Declaration of Truthfulness
text: The exporter of any goods shall present to the proper customs officer a shipping bill or bill of export. The exporter shall at the foot of the document make and subscribe to a declaration as to the truth of its contents. Discrepancies in quantity, valuation, or classification are punishable under Section 113 of the Customs Act.

rule_title: Letter of Undertaking (LUT) / IGST Declaration on Export Invoices
text: Exports from India must be made either under a valid Letter of Undertaking (LUT) without payment of integrated tax (IGST) or on payment of IGST. The export commercial invoice must clearly endorse: 'Supply meant for export on payment of IGST' or 'Supply meant for export under Letter of Undertaking without payment of IGST', along with the ARN of the LUT.

policy_document: FEMA (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations 2015
rule_title: Mandatory 9-Month Export Realization and Repatriation Period
text: The amount representing the full export value of goods shall be realized and repatriated to India through an Authorised Dealer bank within 9 months from the date of export (or 15 months in case of goods exported to an SEZ or warehouse established outside India). Payment must be received in a freely convertible foreign currency or INR through permissible Vostro accounts.

rule_title: Export Policy for Transmission Shafts, Gears, and Mechanical Components (HS 8483)
text: Goods classified under HS Code 8483 (Transmission shafts, cranks, bearing housings, gears, and gearing) are 'Free' for export under ITC (HS) Schedule 2 without requiring a specific DGFT export authorization, provided they are not intended for military, nuclear, or missile applications covered under SCOMET Appendix 3.

rule_title: SCOMET Dual-Use Goods Licensing & End-User Declaration
text: Export of dual-use items, software, and technology classified under SCOMET list is restricted. If equipment has dual commercial and military applications, the exporter must obtain a SCOMET authorization license from DGFT and present an authenticated End-User Certificate (EUC) from the foreign buyer.

policy_document: Customs Valuation (Determination of Value of Export Goods) Rules 2007
text: The transaction value of export goods shall be the Free on Board (FOB) price actually paid or payable. Where commercial invoices are billed on CIF or CFR Incoterms, freight and insurance charges must be separately documented and deducted to determine assessable FOB export value on the Shipping Bill.
